mappings.note: A definition of endemism -- species restricted to one geographical region -- which is a fact about how life is distributed across the biosphere, C2.8. Not C5.2: this item stops at the definition and asks for no conservation judgement, which is what separates it from the hotspot items.

Recall of which organisms occur naturally where (polar bear is the odd one out) -- distribution across Earth's climatic zones, C2.8. Shares the previous item's home honestly: both are endemism-as-distribution, with no conservation decision to push either toward C5.2.

The hotspot criterion has two halves and the second is habitat loss, so the item is about conservation priority, not distribution -- C5.2 names 'conservation of biodiversity' among its case studies. That second half is what moves this off C2.8, where the bare endemism items sit.

Ram Bux Singh and India's first scientifically designed biogas plant -- C6.1, India's contributions to the subject matter being studied. Not C-4.1-LO-2 despite the concept tag being the ecological role of Monera: no organism is classified and no kingdom is named in the item at all.

Today's diversity as the product of small variations accumulating over vast time under environmental pressure -- C4.5's natural selection and its consequences. Not C4.2-LO-9: nothing about classification systems is asked, only about how the diversity itself arose.

Tests which of three candidate criteria are fundamental: cell type and cell number in, habitat out. That is C-4.1-LO-1's 'number of cells present, cellular organisation'. Not C-4.1-LO-2: no organism is placed in any group, the item is purely about the criteria.

Chronology of the classification systems from Aristotle to Whittaker -- LO-9 is the only row covering why one system gave way to the next. Not C7.1: these are historical systems, not the current understanding.

Attribution of each system to its author (Linnaeus, Haeckel, Copeland, Whittaker). Same single home as the chronology item above -- the succession of kingdom systems has one outcome in this curriculum and there is no honest way to split attribution from sequence.

Three of the four options are cell type, level of organisation and mode of nutrition -- C-4.1-LO-1's three named characteristics exactly; presence of blood is the intruder. C4.2-LO-9 was considered and rejected: the item never discusses the move between systems, only which characteristics count.

A branching flowchart resolved into Monera and Fungi -- classification into the five kingdoms on cellular organisation plus nutrition, C-4.1-LO-2. Not C-4.1-LO-1: the features are given by the flowchart, the work is naming the kingdoms.

The assertion is a grouping claim (bacteria and cyanobacteria in Monera, C-4.1-LO-2); the reason is a characteristic claim and is the half that is false (eukaryotic, not prokaryotic, C-4.1-LO-1). An assertion-reason item whose two halves genuinely sit on two rows.

Cyanobacteria identified by the ecological role they played -- C-4.1-LO-2 explicitly includes 'ecological role' -- and the role in question is oxygenating the early atmosphere, which is C2.8's biosphere-atmosphere interrelationship. Not C4.5: no selection or inherited change is argued.
Unicellular plus true nucleus plus a cell wall yields Protista -- placement, C-4.1-LO-2. Same row as the flowchart item because both hand over the features and ask only for the kingdom.

Two stem cross-sections separated by the presence of conducting tissue -- body organisation, so the C4.2 competency, which is where the whole plant-division family sits for want of any plant-division outcome. Not C4.5: the item names a structural difference, it does not argue an evolutionary sequence.

The analogy is completed with two characteristics, multicellular and heterotrophic -- cell number and mode of nutrition, C-4.1-LO-1. Not C-4.1-LO-2: Fungi is given in the stem, so no placement is being made.

Statements 1 to 3 are characteristics to be judged true or false (C-4.1-LO-1: multicellular eukaryote, chitin not cellulose, not autotrophic), while statement 4 is the saprophytic ecological role, which is the clause C-4.1-LO-2 adds. That fourth statement is what separates this from the Monera-Fungi analogy item.

The item states its own basis: evolutionary sequence plus dependence on water for sexual reproduction, and gymnosperms are odd because they escaped that dependence. C4.5 ('changes in structure, and function of organisms') rather than C4.2, which is where the plant items whose discriminator is body organisation sit.

LO-15 names lichens verbatim -- 'interactions between members of different groups of organisms' -- and the second half of the item, sensitivity to air quality, reaches C2.8's atmosphere-biosphere link. Not C-4.1-LO-2: alga and fungus are given, no kingdom is assigned.

A four-row feature table read for the ECOLOGICAL ROLE of decomposer, which is the clause that distinguishes C-4.1-LO-2 from C-4.1-LO-1. The chitin wall and heterotrophy are the route; the decomposer role is what is actually asked for.

The 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' label, tested against a false reason about deserts. The substance of the answer is the bryophyte body plan and its incomplete move to land, so C4.2 with the rest of the plant-division family; not C4.5, since no evolutionary ranking or advantage is argued.

Ordering five plant groups by increasing structural complexity (C4.2, levels of organisation) AND by successful adaptation to terrestrial life (C4.5). One of the few plant items where both halves of the split are explicitly demanded by the stem, so both are cited.

Fern against moss on one internal structural advancement, the vascular tissue. C4.2 as for the rest of the body-organisation half of the plant family; not C4.5, because the item asks what the fern has, not why that made it succeed.

WEAK FIT on two of four pairs: thallus body and the bryophyte label are body organisation (C4.2), but 'naked seeds on cones' and 'seeds enclosed in fruits' are reproductive characters, and curriculum 82 has no outcome for plant reproduction or seed structure at all. C4.2 is cited for the item as a whole rather than stretching C4.5 over a pure recall match.

Multicellular, heterotrophic, no cell wall -- the characteristics of Animalia, with the cellulose cell wall as the intruder. C-4.1-LO-1. Not C4.2-LO-5: this is a kingdom-level characteristic check, no level of organisation is traced and no phylum is reached.

The notochord's role as the structural precursor of the vertebral column, and as the feature that splits the animal kingdom -- LO-5's 'uses the level reached to place an animal in its phylum', the only phylum-placement row available. Chordata has no outcome of its own, unlike Cnidaria, Annelida and Mollusca.
